[2025-06-24 09:12] derbymanager : From old CM tutorial: *** Attribute: Anticipation Description: How well he anticipates what is about to happen on the pitch.  It's used by defenders and defensive midfielders mostly to prevent passes in the future set offside trap and things like that.  Compared to: *** Attribute: Vision Description: How good he is at recognising players in good positions to pass to.  Which is what creativity will be here, more or less. It'll also be used for through balls one days etc...
[2025-06-24 09:15] derbymanager : ---  As for the build up... The main purpose of the build up phase is to see who gets the ball to start the action. That's it. What happens after that is far more important.  The idea is that the better team gets to start more actions (and worse team has to rely on counters more). At least in theory. So this change aims to make it so. If you have world class players and your opponent lower division players, I want you to start 30 actions while he starts 10. Then counters can make that more "even" in some cases, but generally speaking, you want some experienced players in your team to start your actions...

So unless we're playing an infinite clicker game there needs to be a way for younger players to overtake older ones. Hence, older players need to lose skills, so younger ones could become better. Sometimes a player drops at 31. Other times at 35. Sometimes he becomes useless in 1 season, other times it takes him 3. I never had a drastic drop in a single season, it was always 1 star per season more or less... But I know it can happen.  So, at some older age they provide mentoring points with which you can train those younger players. The older they are, more mentoring points they provide to make up for not delivering on the pitch. As for training only a specific group of people, yes, one person can mentor only a couple of others. You can't mentor 20 players. That's what real coaches do... So, yes, in theory you could assign a mentor to 1 or 2 people no matter their position... But to avoid a clunky UI I've simplified it like this.  Another point to consider, improving facilities by 1 point costs a dozen million. A single mentor that covers all roles and gives you +3 would be 3x worth that and cost 2M...

[2025-10-19 21:56] pape_susic : I still don't fully understand how tiers, potential and development work, what happened to my boy here? High potential to become solid literally yesterday, reached his peak today...at 21 🤷‍♂️
[2025-10-20 08:08] derbymanager : Tier is just a ranking within the game. top 50 or something players are world class. Their tier is between 9.01 and 10.0 (the best one has 10, the 51st one has 9). Next 200 are elites with tier between 7.01 and 9.0... Your player is a promising youngster which means his tier is between 2.01 and 3.0.  Since it is a ranking, if he doesn't grow at all, someone else who does grow will overtake him and push him down in terms of tier. Even if he does grow, someone else might be growing faster and still overtake him.  Finally, based on his potential and where exactly within his tier he is, there is some guesswork where he might end up. If he is at 2.05 he might get to 2.95 but still stay in the same tier (since the next one is at 3.01+). Since the game doesn't know how everyone else will grow, it's really just a guess. No guarantees whatsoever. He might even grow to reach higher tier if the game's guess is wrong (which can easily be the case). But, in any case, it gives you some hint where he might end up, approximately). You can be sure he won't grow to become an elite player but somewhere around solid is reasonable.
[2025-10-20 08:17] derbymanager : Development, on the other hand, depends on potential. Every player has "current power" (a calculation of how good he is right now in terms of skills) and a potential power that says how far can he grow. Potential is adjusted by club fit and the competition where he plays (team tier). No player will become a world class player while playing in 4th division. He needs to go to 1st division to become world class (assuming he has potential to even reach that far). Club fit is in there to make sure that potential isn't revealed simply by looking when someone started to complain about training.  Still, in a d4 team, a player with best potential will usually be able to grow more than the one with low potential. From manager's point of view, without metagaming, you would see a player grow and reach highest price in your team and he would ask to leave. You could then decide whether you want to sell him for the money or to keep him for his skills...
[2025-10-20 08:33] poletz : And with metagaming? 😀
[2025-10-20 09:00] derbymanager : you can try to understand whether something happens because of club fit, potential, or just luck, and then you have the same decision to make 🙂

[2025-12-30 14:07] furysk : Training happiness is a bit meh/broken.  I’d argue the issue here is carrying both low stadium and low sponsorship, though part of that was bad luck on the facility reduction.
[2025-12-30 15:02] furysk : May not want to hear it from me but I’d say salary increase by expectations are a massive bait to ruin one’s financials.  The team balance sheet at 100% is better off than at 105-120%, the team doesn’t get any additional dollars per win or sponsors to cover that.  The second issue is team expected revenues is based on a higher number than what your attendance ends up at.  So if you have a 50k stadium you might see 500k in stadium revenues instead of 400k, which on the balance sheet means the team doesn’t look to eat into facility upkeep to cover the fact that financially you might not be making all that money in reality.
[2025-12-30 16:11] furysk : At a glance, sponsors if you increase no wages would get you 30k less facilities reduction.  You’d pay more maintenance but you’d gain more sponsorship than you’d gain in maintenance cost.  I don’t know for certain on stadium what you’d gain. My guess would seats at 2.5 would get you 40-50k less maintenance (80-100k revenue roughly in estimated stadium value minus the cost of upkeep at a level higher).  The solution probably isn't great, but i would: Look for 55-75k in salary to offload Look to upgrade stadium. Live with the rest of the difference.  IMHO getting it to about 85-95k in bleed would put you in position to be competitive still, would make it to where you'd have to have 3-3.5 seasons in between facility issues in terms of the pace they'd decline.  prey it hits movement, and reinvest a future update in sponsors.  Once your team's Broadcast + Sponsors - Wages = 0 roughly, the problems will stop.  Yeah, you'll have teams outspending you or spending every dollar, but they'll suffer from the same problems as you do right now (not enough cash to offset maintenance).

[2026-08-22 19:17] derbymanager : <@94676029846593536> I really, really appreciate people that go this deep into the game, it's soooo beneficial for me. You are right, but I think one part of the picture is missing.  There are a couple of things that work as anchor points in the game. For example, 1st most popular team gets tier 10, 50th gets tier 9. Places 2-49 are distributed proportionally to their popularity compared to the 1st and 5th.  Popularity, that determines tier, is tied to the league you're in. 1st place in d4 is IDK tier 200 or something like that. But generally speaking you can't go much higher than 200 in d4.   And tier + league define revenues, more or less. So we can treat these as static values. D4 teams get between on average X money, or at most Y money. Whatever we need. The X and Y are static since the beginning basically.  However, what's not static are players. Their values and demands are relative to their power (and a bunch of other modifiers but we can ignore these, the quality highly correlates to price). And, over time, the average quality of players increased. Training is too good (if I nerf it, people are unhappy), schools got improved (people were unhappy before), and just the general churn of shitty players makes it so that the average value of d4 team has increased significantly compared to the season 1 (or whichever older season you want to take as benchmark).  So, average player quality increased, and with that average demands have increased... but the finances are constant, as I mentioned earlier.  Giving more money to d4 teams is counter productive IMO. It leads towards inflation, while I wanted to anchor the system somehow so that I don't have to inflate every other financial thing in the game too. The fact that teams are having salary issues and struggling is because teams in d4 consist of bigger teams that have dropped down and teams that have maxed out their squads so it's hard to compete with a normal squad...
[2026-08-22 19:25] derbymanager : I'll try to dig out some numbers from backups but I'm pretty certain that's where the issue lies. Average player today is simply more powerful than the average player 20 seasons ago, while the finances are basically the same. Sure, I made a ton of changes and they contribute to the situation too (as you said, you can't really sell 5 players and replace them with 5k-salary palyers from school anymore), but the core of the issue lies in the fact that the player values are not anchored while the rest of the game is.
